data.title: Should Long Term Sales Outlook Require Action From Novartis (SWX:NOVN) Investors?
data.description:
• Novartis issued new long term guidance through 2031, targeting around 5% annual net sales growth at constant currencies, alongside extensive oncology, immunology and cardiovascular pipeline updates, including fresh clinical data and a new FDA approval for Cosentyx in polymyalgia rheumatica.
  • Management is leaning on a broader mix of specialty medicines, from Cosentyx label expansions to remibrutinib and radioligand therapies, to help offset upcoming loss of exclusivity pressures while maintaining a core operating margin goal of at least 40% by 2029.
  • We will explore how Novartis' 5% long term sales guidance interacts with its existing growth narrative built around specialty medicines.

Scan how Novartis is repositioning around specialty medicines, then size up other potential compounders with a similar profile using our hand picked 236 high quality undervalued stocks

Novartis Investment Narrative Recap

To own Novartis, you effectively need to buy into a long haul specialty medicines story where a broad mix of oncology, immunology and cardiovascular drugs can offset loss of exclusivity and support the long term 5% constant currency net sales growth target. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St already leans on that idea, with newer therapies and cost discipline doing the heavy lifting.

The fresh 2026 to 2031 guidance largely reinforces that script rather than rewrites it. The most important near term swing factor remains how sharply upcoming patent cliffs hit in 2026 and how quickly newer products, including Cosentyx extensions and radioligand therapies, can fill the gap. Pipeline setbacks and margin pressure from Xolair erosion still frame the key risks.

The recent US FDA approval of Cosentyx for polymyalgia rheumatica ties directly into this specialty medicines pivot. It adds another immune mediated indication where Novartis already has commercial infrastructure, which can matter when the group is trying to offset expected 2026 loss of exclusivity pressure while still aiming for a core operating margin of at least 40% by 2029.

For catalysts, that approval sits alongside the broader oncology and hematology pipeline updates and the long term 5% sales growth ambition through 2031. Execution now hinges on turning these label expansions and late stage data readouts into durable prescription demand without letting safety monitoring, competitive entries or pricing pressure dilute the contribution that investors are counting on from Cosentyx and related specialty brands.

What The Long Term Novartis Targets Assume

Analysts are effectively sketching out what Novartis has to deliver for the specialty medicines story to line up with today’s valuation. The forecasts imply that revenue needs to compound at 6.3% a year over the next few years, while profit margins rise from 17.5% today to 27.4% by around 2029. That is a large jump in profitability, so it leans heavily on the mix shift toward higher margin oncology, immunology and cardiovascular drugs alongside ongoing cost work.

On earnings, the consensus view points to profit of about US$18.8b by 2029 compared with US$10.0b today. That is roughly an 88% increase in absolute earnings, even before considering the projected 1.57% annual reduction in the share count. For you as an investor, the gap between the bullish US$23.5b and bearish US$16.3b estimates underlines how much of the Novartis story is still about execution on the late stage pipeline and on recent launches such as radioligand therapies and remibrutinib.

Valuation expectations flow directly from those operating targets. The analyst framework assumes Novartis would be earning US$18.8b on revenues of US$68.8b in 2029, with the stock trading on a P/E of 16.6x. That multiple is lower than the 30.6x implied today and below the 37.8x currently quoted for the US Pharmaceuticals industry in the report. This means the scenario is not built on multiple expansion. It is built on earnings compounding while the P/E compresses closer to a sector discount.

Price targets reflect that fairly measured setup. The consensus sits at CHF126.97, not far from the current CHF133.78 share price, with a range from CHF99.70 to CHF179.46 among covering analysts. With the average target only 5.4% below where Novartis trades today, the market is being told that a lot of the specialty medicines and margin story is already in the price. Your job is to decide whether the 6.3% revenue growth path, the margin lift toward 27.4% and the US$18.8b earnings outcome feel achievable, conservative or optimistic given the patent cliffs and the pipeline mix.

Novartis' current analyst narrative points to revenues of about US$68.8b and earnings of roughly US$18.8b by 2029, which assumes 6.3% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$8.8b from the current US$10.0b level.

data.title: Dual Drug Approvals Could Be A Big Moment For Sanofi Stock (ENXTPA:SAN)
data.description:
• Sanofi has secured two major regulatory milestones, with the European Commission approving its Vero cell based rabies vaccine VaxRabeo for pre and post exposure use across all ages, and the US FDA authorizing Infilbray for neurological manifestations of Type 3 Gaucher disease in eligible adults and children.
  • These green lights expand Sanofi's reach in both global vaccination programs and rare disease treatment. They add fresh products in areas where clinical need is high and where the group has already built meaningful manufacturing, regulatory and commercial know how.
  • The focus now turns to how Sanofi's existing investment narrative intersects with new Infilbray approval momentum in its rare disease portfolio.

Sanofi Investment Narrative Recap

To own Sanofi, you need to be comfortable with a large pharma group that is reshaping around higher margin prescription drugs and vaccines while carrying mixed recent profitability. According to Szock, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the appeal rests on solid cash generation and a dividend that has historically looked robust, even as one off items weighed on the latest reported margins.

The fresh FDA approval for Infilbray looks most relevant for catalysts because it fits directly into Sanofi’s rare disease and neurology focus that investors already watch closely. It is a once daily oral option for neurological manifestations of Type 3 Gaucher disease, a space with few alternatives, and it runs across both adult and pediatric patients.

Operationally, this adds a new product in a highly specialized area where treatment decisions are concentrated among a small group of physicians, so execution is measurable but unforgiving. Safety warnings, including suicidal ideation and paediatric lens issues, keep clinical risk on the table, and uptake will sit alongside regulator reviews in the EU and Japan as investors track the next leg of news flow.

On the latest view, the narrative fair value of Arista Networks at $169.91 sits only slightly above the last close of $167.62. That small gap puts the focus squarely on how sustainable the current AI buildout looks rather than on any big pricing mismatch.

Arista reported Q3 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 58.5%, and forecast Q4 revenue between $3.9 billion and $4 billion. The headline is strong. One table in the 10-Q adds a detail worth holding next to it. Deferred revenue fell in the quarter, from $6,865.9 million to $6,839.5 million. A year earlier it rose $624.5 million. Revenue recognized from the opening deferred balance was $1,715.0 million, about 47% of Q3 revenue, against $699.7 million, about 30%, in Q3 2025. That balance holds multi-year support contracts and product deferrals tied to acceptance clauses. When large customers accept deployments, revenue comes out of it, so part of Q3's growth likely came from earlier shipments clearing rather than only from new orders. New deferrals were still $1,688.6 million, up from $1,324.2 million a year earlier. The balance is being refilled, just not faster than it's being drawn down. The CFO warned against reading one quarter too closely: "the deferred balance can move significantly on a quarterly basis, independent of underlying business drivers." I agree, and this isn't a bear case. Management's first look at 2027 is 38% to 40% growth, to about $18.5 billion. Arista expects $8.6 billion of revenue from remaining performance obligations, about 91% of it within two years, and purchase commitments rose to $11.4 billion from $9.7 billion in Q2. What I'd watch in the Q4 report is whether the balance grows again. If it does alongside revenue of $3.9 billion or more, demand is outrunning acceptances. If it falls again, growth is leaning harder on the balance, and the 2027 range carries more of the story. The Q3 call and both filings are here.
